acceptanceCriteria: test-read-scopes-check (or a sibling) fails when a declared package's non-test module dependencies are not covered by its read scope, at least for packages whose tests run go list
Proven on a synthetic omission that reproduces the #1288 case
The test failure message includes go list's stderr, not a bare exit status
body: Batch PR #1288 (CI run 39376177909, go-product-shard 3): TestGitNotesFetchesNothing failed with a bare 'gitnotes_test.go:296: exit status 1' from 'go list -deps .'. The cause: #1279 (V1-1292) made internal/gitnotes import internal/cem/verify, which pulls in internal/cem/sim, and neither directory was in the package's .corvint/test-read-scopes.json entry. Under Landlock, go list cannot read them. 'make test-read-scopes-check' passed locally, and the test passes locally without confinement. Fixed in batch commit 3d220661a by adding both directories. V1-1736 (TestCCEV0015CoreBoundary, bare exit status 1 from go list -deps) is probably the same class. Expected: the check fails when a declared package's non-standard transitive imports fall outside its read scope, or when a declared package's test shells out to go list. Actual: the check does not compare scopes with the import graph.
